Israel weighs extended voting hours, additional polling day amid security concerns
Israel’s Central Elections Committee is considering extended voting hours or an additional day of voting if security emergencies disrupt the upcoming Knesset election
With elections for the 26th Knesset exactly two weeks away, Israel’s Central Elections Committee and police are preparing for potential security emergencies on election day.
Sources told i24NEWS the committee is considering extending voting hours or, if necessary, holding an additional day of voting should a security incident disrupt the election.
Regional election committees have already been instructed to coordinate with those responsible for polling station buildings to ensure that protected spaces are available, directions are clearly marked and emergency instructions can be communicated to voters.
Police are also preparing for the possibility of holding elections during wartime. At least one exercise testing that scenario took place earlier this week.
The Central Elections Committee said it is preparing for all scenarios, including emergencies, to ensure the election is conducted in accordance with the law. Given the security situation on the home front, it said it is required to map protected spaces and review security measures at polling locations.

UN condemns Black Sea drone attacks, warns of risks to global food supplies

04:35:26 KST

The United Nations has condemned drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea, warning that escalating threats to civilian shipping could disrupt global food supply chains, drive up commodity prices and endanger seafarers.
“We of course condemn attacks on civilian ships, especially the most recent one that took place off the coast of Bulgaria,” UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres’ spokesperson, Stephane Dujarric, told reporters on Tuesday.
Dujarric said attacks on ships carrying grain and other essential commodities had increased, with consequences for prices in markets worldwide.
He also drew comparisons with maritime threats in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, praising seafarers who continue to sustain global trade despite operating in dangerous conditions.
Two vessels struck off Bulgaria
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 issued a distress call early Tuesday after three aerial drones struck its deck and side, about 18 nautical miles east of Byala.
All 15 crew members aboard the Ukrainian-owned vessel were safely evacuated to the Bulgarian port of Varna, according to Radev.
A second ship was struck about 17 nautical miles east of Krapets and subsequently sank, the prime minister said. One sailor was rescued.
The incidents add to concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, a vital corridor for regional trade and agricultural exports.
UN raises alarm over maritime security
The UN’s warning highlights the broader economic risks posed by attacks on civilian vessels, particularly those transporting food and other essential goods.
Disruptions to shipping routes can increase transport costs, delay deliveries and put additional pressure on commodity markets.
Dujarric’s remarks also underscored the dangers faced by maritime crews as security threats affect key waterways used by international commerce.

Ex-gang leader sentenced to 40 years to life in prison for Tupac Shakur murder
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:32:00 UTC
04:32:00 KST

A former gang leader was sentenced to 40 years to life in prison on Tuesday for orchestrating the 1996 drive-by shooting death of hip-hop star Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas, capping the prosecution of a long-unsolved murder that shaped the golden age of rap music.
Duane "Keffe D" Davis, 63, found guilty of first-degree murder in August, received the penalty during a hearing in a Las Vegas courtroom.
Until Davis' 2023 arrest, the killing of Shakur, shot dead in the passenger seat of an SUV driven by his record executive, Marion "Suge" Knight, had stood for nearly three decades as one of America's most notorious cold cases.
The murder, which silenced one of rap's most commercially successful and influential artists, heightened the image of violence permeating 1990s hip-hop culture while stoking the infamous East Coast-West Coast "gangsta" rap feud of the era.
Despite Davis' conviction, the question of who pulled the trigger in the fatal shooting of the 25-year-old rap legend has never been conclusively decided.
Davis was tried and convicted for masterminding the murder to avenge the beating of his nephew by Shakur and members of the rapper's entourage inside the MGM Grand casino on the Las Vegas Strip on September 7, 1996.
Davis has said he would appeal his conviction.
Fatal shooting sparked by casino brawl
The clash at the casino stemmed from hostility between two Los Angeles-area street gangs - the South Side Compton Crips, of which Davis was the self-described leader, and Mob Piru, associated with Shakur, Knight, and their music label, Death Row Records.
Members of both groups were in Las Vegas that night to see a world heavyweight title boxing match between Mike Tyson and Bruce Seldon.
Within hours of the casino brawl, Davis ushered his nephew and two other associates into a white Cadillac and went looking for Shakur and Knight, determined to settle scores, according to an account Davis later gave police in an unrelated investigation and that prosecutors cited during his murder trial.
Davis said he passed a gun to the two men seated behind him in the Cadillac, one of whom opened fire through the window when they caught up with, and pulled alongside, Knight and Shakur’s vehicle in traffic.
Shakur was struck four times and died in a hospital six days later. Knight, who suffered a minor injury from a bullet fragment that grazed his head, is now serving a 28-year prison term on an unrelated voluntary manslaughter conviction.
Authorities initially lacked sufficient evidence for charges despite suspicions
Authorities said they long believed Davis was involved in Shakur's killing but lacked sufficient evidence to charge him.
That changed when he went public with his story in media appearances and a memoir that, along with tapes of his secret meetings with investigators, formed the bulk of the prosecution’s murder case.
In his book, Compton Street Legend, Davis himself wrote that he was considered a suspect in the murders of both Shakur and Christopher Wallace, a rival rapper.
Wallace, who performed as the Notorious B.I.G. under the New York-based Bad Boy Entertainment label, was shot dead in Los Angeles in March 1997.
Although the Wallace killing remains unsolved, there has long been speculation that he was gunned down in retaliation for Shakur's killing months earlier.
While Davis was never accused of actually firing the shots that killed Shakur - Nevada law allows someone to be charged with murder as a participant in the crime - prosecutors have never named a suspected gunman.
All three other men in the Cadillac with Davis that night have since died.

Pope Leo XIV hospitalized ahead of lung surgery
Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome’s Agostino Gemelli University Hospital ahead of surgery on Tuesday afternoon to remove a “small, localized nodule” from his lung, Qazinform News Agency reports, citing Vatican News.
According to the Holy See Press Office, the operation will be performed by the hospital’s thoracic surgery team, led by Professor Stefano Margaritora. An update on the Pope’s condition is expected on Tuesday evening.
Speaking to journalists on Monday, Holy See Press Office Director Matteo Bruni said the nodule had been detected during routine medical examinations. The Pope is expected to remain in hospital for about a week after the procedure.
Pope Leo held all his scheduled audiences on Monday morning before arriving at the hospital at 1:07 p.m. People gathered outside, applauding and calling out greetings as his vehicle entered the hospital grounds.
The Pope greeted hospital leaders and briefly approached several patients, including people in wheelchairs, before entering the building.
Messages of support continued to arrive from churches and political leaders around the world. Some religious sisters gathered in the hospital’s St. John Paul II Chapel to pray for the Pope. Cardinal Baldassare Reina, the Pope’s Vicar General for the Diocese of Rome, was scheduled to lead the Rosary there at 6 p.m.
Elena Beccalli, rector of the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, also conveyed the university community’s support and prayers during the Pope’s hospitalization.
“As he is admitted to the hospital, we accompany him with our prayers, mindful of the close bond between our university and the Agostino Gemelli University Hospital Foundation,” she told Vatican News.
Earlier, Qazinform News Agency reported that Pope Leo XIV would undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a small nodule in his lung.

Humanity without family is unlikely to remain humaity
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:25:19 UTC
04:25:19 KST

Humanity without family is unlikely to remain humaity
In the first quarter of the 21st century, planetary humanity underwent an enormous transformation, one that is more accurately described not merely as historical, but as anthropological, because it alters the very mode of being of the species Homo sapiens. What is striking is not only the evolutionary scale of this transformation, but also the speed with which it occurred. Very quickly, literally within the span of one generation, humanity shifted toward a family-less way of life.
Let us grasp the meaning of what has happened. Human beings of our species were formed, multiplied, and spread across the planet in tightly knit kin groups that expanded into tribes while simultaneously dividing into more compact and distinct families. Aristotle therefore did not invent, but simply described the social nature of the rational human being and called the family the first – that is, the basic and foundational – form of human association.
Incidentally, Aristotle, long before Jesus Christ, also warned of the existential threat to humanity posed by chrematistics (Ancient Greek χρηματιστική, money-making, from χρήματα, money), or capitalism, in modern terms. He regarded chrematistics as a perverted form of economic activity, contrary to human nature and destructive of society, including the family. Then, some three hundred years later, Jesus Christ came and taught that worship of Mammon leads people away from God – with all the consequences that follow.
Two thousand years have passed. Let us omit the details and focus on the essential point. Political scientist Francis Fukuyama called the end of the 20th century the end of world history. Only frivolous people can think Fukuyama was simply inventing things. The state of global humanity at the turn of the 20th and 21st centuries was described by sociologist Zygmunt Bauman as individualized and “liquid,” because all social institutions and concepts had lost their certainty and obligatory force. But Bauman had not yet witnessed the annihilation of the family as the matrix of humanity.
Let us trace the chronology of disintegration. The so-called sexual revolution of the baby-boomer generation in the late 1960s, affirming postmodern values of individual self-expression and hedonism, cast aside religious “narratives” that is, commandments – and severed the root tradition of family life. After that, churches in Western Europe rapidly emptied, and both marriage and childbearing went into decline. The United States, owing to the conservatism of its heartland and the inflow of Latin American immigrants, has lagged slightly behind, but is moving in the same direction, and the process is accelerating. This is clearly visible in the following data. Through the entire first half and middle of the 20th century until the 1970s, the annual marriage rate averaged 10–11 per thousand people, but then began to decline, repeatedly reaching historic lows.
Statistics on marriages and divorces in the 21st century for one hundred countries of the world are collected here. In the 2000s, the United States already had fewer than 8 marriages per thousand population. In Russia at the start of the century, the marriage rate stood at 7.5 per thousand, and in China at 7.1. In Europe, Latin America, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore, the number of marriages was shrinking even faster. As a result, the average marriage rate across one hundred countries fell below 6 in the 2000s – 5.96 marriages per thousand people.
Over the first quarter of the 21st century, the global marriage rate fell to unprecedented lows: today the average indicator across one hundred countries is noticeably below 5, at 4.83 marriages per thousand people. The number of marriages has declined in 81 of those 100 countries. In Japan, South Korea, and Australia, the figure has fallen to 4; in Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, and Britain it is below 3.5 marriages per thousand people. In South America, once considered a bastion of Catholicism, and in black Africa, which is regarded as such today, marriage rates are even lower because most cohabiting couples neither marry in church nor formally register their unions.
At the same time, in 70 out of 100 countries, the fall in the marriage rate is accompanied by a rise in the number of divorces. In 65 countries, the number of divorces already exceeds one-third of the number of marriages, including 30 countries where divorces amount to half or more of marriages.
The result of these processes is a rapid decline in the number of two-parent families with children. Looking at 73 countries, for which detailed information is available, we can see that only in 7 of the 73 countries does the share of families with children exceed 40% of all households, and in only 4 more countries do families with children account for more than one-third of households. In 44 countries – that is, in the overwhelming majority of countries for which there are statistics – the number of families with children amounts to less than a quarter of all households. In the United States, the family share has fallen below 20%, while in Europe it is even lower, down to 16–14% in most cases, and even as low as 10% in Lithuania and Denmark.
Thus, the increasingly informatized and progressive society of postmodernity, having begun with the assertion of individualism and the shrinking of childbearing, entered in the 21st century a phase of radical atomization with the final disintegration of humanity’s family way of life. The cosmic meaning and scale of this metamorphosis lies in the fact that the species Homo sapiens, once having become the demiurge of meaningful life, once overcoming the deathliness of the material world through the life of the human race, is now renouncing its anti-entropic mission as too burdensome. For the mission of humanity, in essence, is labor and faith – and these are exactly what “progress” wears away. Unceasing labor and stubborn faith in the higher meaning of continuing the human line are being replaced by the comfort of self-sufficient individuals, a comfort that ensures the comfortable euthanasia of the species Homo sapiens, fully in keeping with the “scientific picture” of entropy in the material world.
The transition to a childless and family-less way of life has produced a tectonic break in global population dynamics, from a fading demographic explosion to demographic implosion. In 2026, the world’s total fertility rate fell below 2.20, the level necessary for simple replacement. The population of the planet is still growing by inertia of age structure, but if current trends persist, it will peak at roughly 9 billion around 2056, after which it will begin to decline. In fact, however, the real drop in birth rates around the world has recently outpaced all scientific forecasts.
The cited article by economists Jesús Fernández-Villaverde (University of Pennsylvania) and Patrick Norrick (Northwestern University) describes the global demographic collapse as a natural process driven by “modernity” itself: prolonged education, career-building, the high cost of preparing a child for life, weakened kinship networks, and expanding opportunities for women outside the family.
Let us speak plainly. The notion of the objective inevitability of the destruction of the family matrix and the accelerated depopulation of humanity, replicated in countless academic and analytical publications, is a mental projection of the power of globalist elites advancing and implementing a strategy of elitist transhumanism and the divergence of the species Homo sapiens.
Let us cite two counterarguments that refute the hypothesis that humanity’s atomization and depopulation are exclusively natural processes.
First, this hypothesis ignores the anti-religious (“anticlerical”), anti-national (“cosmopolitan”), anti-traditional and anti-historical (“progressive” and “postmodern”), and now also anti-family and anti-humanist (“transhumanist”) cultural revolution that was designed and systematically carried out by capitalist elites as Western civilization transformed and the Western world-system of capital accumulation and concentration expanded globally. It is precisely this global expansion and the total domination of postmodern “values” – value relativism and asocial individualism – that has produced the globality and speed of humanity’s dehumanization.
Second, this family-less and childless “modernity,” on closer inspection, turns out to be heterogeneous – there are exceptions to the dominant trend, and they can in no way be called marginal. Such exceptions force us to think and may explain much.
Let us look at the case of Israel. Hardly anyone would dispute that Israel is a modern society and state. Yet in Israel divorces are comparatively rare, while the share of complete families with children among all households (42.5%) is one of the highest in the world and the highest among developed countries; the total fertility rate in Israel remains at an ideal level, holding steady at 3 births per woman.
Israel’s demographic distinctiveness finds its explanation in the geopolitical context of the emergence and existence of the modern Zionist state. That context is clearly characterized by acute ethnic competition with a religious accent, which in the case of the Jewish state is inseparable from global capitalism. Ethno-religious separation on the basis of chosenness, tied to global capital accumulation, is precisely what constitutes the logic of social apartheid and species divergence.
In this connection, it is also worth noting that the survival of the family institution under today’s conditions has a very clear class dimension. Data from the United States, for example, show that the decline in marriage is concentrated primarily among the poor majority (60%) of American society. Among the richest 20% of Americans, the marriage rate has changed little over recent decades and remains at around 80%. Therefore, the “marriage crisis” is not total, but is occurring at the expense of the lower classes, which constitute the social majority. In other words, marriage and family are ceasing to be a universal human norm and are now becoming an elite privilege of the wealthy and educated minority.
What emerges is the following picture. The crisis of sociality has become total and, following social structures of various historical ages, has now struck the root, matrix institution of human common life – the family. Under the banner of unstoppable progress, the withering of the family has spread across, homogenized, and in effect eliminated almost all civilizations, reaching its greatest destructive force in the most developed countries with the highest standard of living, where complete families with children have become a disappearing rarity, and where former national states have been replaced by conglomerates of populations ever more alienated from historical tradition, ever more atomized, and increasingly lacking independence. Meaningful exceptions to the general trend are visible only in Israel and among the uppermost stratum of global elites.
This evolution of humanity fully corresponds to the strategy of transhumanism, in which the aspirations of the global elite are formulated – today, the dominant and ruling groups of globally corporate and state-monopoly capitalism. In mass consciousness, the transhumanist strategy has been projected in the form of the UN concept of sustainable development. Over several decades, through the system of globalist centers of influence, mainstream expertise, education, and mass media, humanity’s consent to population contraction has been conceptualized, implanted, and implemented as the main condition and criterion of sustainable development. The mental and psychological support for the voluntary castration of the human race has been the economically compelled and mass-culture-enforced transition to a childless, family-less, individualized lifestyle of human units living “for themselves.”
At the same time, the progressive aging and shrinking of the Homo sapiens population is occurring primarily at the expense of the economically unstable and increasingly indebted mass strata – the majority of humanity. Meanwhile, the elites that possess capital and social power are, on the contrary, accumulating and monopolizing the existential resources of life itself, including longer life expectancy, family continuity, and reproductive capacity. In this way, globally interconnected elite communities have neutralized the threat of mass uprising and acquired a new quality of chosenness, cultivating not only property superiority but existential, inherited species superiority over the discarded and withering species of so-called Homo sapiens.

Diplomatic tensions flared again between India and China after Beijing strongly opposed India’s decision to officially map and standardise 28 places in Ladakh, including some in Aksai China, and reaffirmed that it does not recognise the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh.In a swift rebuttal, New Delhi reiterated no amount of Chinese denial can change the established fact that the Ladakh UT is an integral and inalienable part of India.According to the ministry of home affairs (MHA), which announced the standardisation in a press release on October 2, identifying the places/ geographical features formally on the Survey of India map was aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated the same, saying the MHA statement was self-explanatory.“The announcement mentions that the twenty-eight (28) places/features located in the UT of Ladakh have been identified with standard place and feature names on the official map of Survey of India, and it has been done in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh and local stakeholders,” he said.The Chinese foreign ministry described the Indian move as illegal saying it doesn’t change the fact that the western sector of the China-India boundary belongs to China.
“China has never recognized the so-called Union Territory of Ladakh unilaterally and illegally established by India, and firmly opposes the so-called standardized names publicised by India,” said spokesperson Mao Ning.However, China itself has renamed places in Arunachal Pradesh on at least half a dozen occasions in the past 10 years, including twice in 2026, to reinforce its claim over the Indian state.The fresh cartographic tussle comes in the middle of the ongoing normalisation of the bilateral relationship after a military standoff in eastern Ladakh. The Chinese response was a throwback to its statement in 2019 – a day after India revoked the special status of J&K in 2019 – accusing New Delhi of undermining China's territorial sovereignty by unilaterally changing its domestic law and establishing Ladakh UT.“Such practice is unacceptable and will not come into force,” it had then said, warning India to exercise prudence in words and deeds on the boundary question. It was perhaps no coincidence that the military conflict in eastern Ladakh started 8 months later.Beijing maintains that it has always opposed India's inclusion of “Chinese territory in the western sector of the China-India boundary into its administrative jurisdiction”. For China,
Aksai Chin in the western sector remains of critical importance as it links the politically sensitive autonomous regions of Xinjiang and Tibet.However, the border situation has remained stable since PM Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping met in Kazan in 2024. India and China have since held 3 rounds of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question, with the last round in August resulting in 8 outcomes, including a decision to advance talks for an “early and substantial” harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.

“Let Ukrainians Do What They’ve Been Very Good At”: Trump’s Ex-Envoy Backs Strikes on Russia
Ukraine should be free to strike targets inside Russia in response to Moscow’s war, former US special envoy for Ukraine Keith Kellogg told Bloomberg on October 12.
Kellogg, a retired lieutenant general who served as President Donald Trump’s special envoy for Ukraine until the end of 2025, argued that Kyiv should not allow Russia to maintain safe areas from which it can continue attacks.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Invoking his experience during the Vietnam War, Kellogg stated that one should not permit “sanctuaries” for an opponent during a conflict.
“Let Ukrainians do what they’ve been very good at,” Kellogg told Bloomberg Television on the sidelines of the Warsaw Security Forum.
He noted that Russia had repeatedly struck Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and argued that Kyiv should be allowed to hit targets inside Russia as it considers necessary.
Kellogg also said that Russia was not winning the war and was instead prolonging it.
His remarks contrast with Trump’s recent call for Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, a campaign Bloomberg described as one of Kyiv’s most effective ways of weakening a key source of funding for Russia’s full-scale invasion.
Kellogg dismissed Trump’s recent comments, including his suggestion that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy should consider stepping aside, as “noise.”
“I think what’s happening is a couple of world leaders—I think they are basically kind of alike,” Kellogg stated. “You know, they’re both kind of stubborn, they both speak their mind.”
The latest dispute followed Trump’s deal with the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, to release Russian diesel onto global markets ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections.
Kellogg argued that the arrangement would not significantly affect the market and was not favorable to Putin.
“He’s trying to capitalize on elections coming up in the US, he’s trying to capitalize on President Trump right now,” Kellogg stated. “And most people see through it.”
Kellogg also described Putin as operating from a position of weakness, citing estimates that Russia had suffered between 1.2 million and 1.5 million casualties during the war, Bloomberg reported.
“The rhetoric will kind of take care of itself,” Kellogg stated. “Look at what’s happening on the ground.”
Days earlier, Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine would halt strikes on Russian oil refineries only if Moscow stopped attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure. He rejected a unilateral pause and insisted that any de-escalation be reciprocal and backed by guarantees.

Cornell Halts Fraternity Parties After Jane Doe’s Lawsuit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:14:51 UTC
04:14:51 KST

Cornell University said on Tuesday that it is barring fraternity houses from hosting parties for the remainder of the academic year in an effort “to strengthen campus safety” after the school faced widespread backlash over its handling of an alleged gang rape by fraternity members in 2024.
Cornell President Michael I. Kotlikoff announced the news in a letter addressed to the campus community, which said that the ban will be effective immediately. He also outlined ways that the university would work to improve how it handles allegations of sexual assault in the future. In addition to strengthening campus safety, he addressed the need to provide better support to survivors—which involves allowing the New York State Police to independently investigate sexual assault allegations—and change the social culture at the university.
Cornell did not immediately respond to questions about the new measures.
The announcement comes about a month after a woman, known as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit against several entities, including Cornell, the Chi Phi fraternity, and seven members of Chi Phi that she alleges sexually assaulted her in 2024. The case has made national headlines, and many people have criticized how Cornell and local authorities handled the incident. Hundreds of students and staff members held a protest on campus earlier this month, with some calling for Kotlikoff to resign and others chanting phrases like “Ban the frats!”
In his letter on Tuesday, Kotlikoff addressed the backlash, saying that his conversations with various members of the campus community and the campus protests “have underscored my deep conviction that we must do better: that the time for meaningful and lasting change at Cornell, and at campuses across the country, is now.”
“I am deeply sorry for the harm Jane Doe suffered in 2024, and appalled that this act of sexual violence occurred within our Cornell community,” Kotlikoff said. “It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action.”
Amid mounting pressure, Cornell’s Board of Trustees announced earlier this month that Sally Yates, a former acting U.S. attorney general, will lead an independent review into how the school handled the case. Kotlikoff also addressed the review in his letter, but said “it is clear that we cannot wait for these findings to take action.” Cooperation with the New York State Police would coincide with the independent review; Kotlikoff said in his letter that investigators will interview survivors who decide to pursue criminal charges and “prepare comprehensive investigative summaries for the appropriate law enforcement agency.”
Kotlikoff said that Interfraternity Council houses will be barred from holding parties and social events, which “will provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life at Cornell to determine whether and how it can safely continue.” He added that the university will have a “zero tolerance” policy if fraternities violate the new rule, and that any fraternity that hosts “an in-house party or social event will receive an immediate emergency suspension.” Cornell has previously said that the Chi Phi fraternity on campus "was closed in 2024 and remains barred from campus."
Other measures that Kotlikoff announced include strengthening support for survivors, such as by adding staffers to the Cornell Office of Civil Rights, and “changing the social culture at Cornell” through several initiatives, such as enhancing “existing education and programming to address the bystander effect.”
“These are first steps toward systemic change on our campus,” Kotlikoff said. “We will take all necessary steps to address the conditions that led to Jane Doe’s experiences, and those of other survivors. Cornell must be a place where safety is not an open question.”

J7 global task force convenes in London to discuss combating global antisemitism
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:13:50 UTC
04:13:50 KST

Leaders of the J7 Large Communities’ Task Force Against Antisemitism gathered in London on Monday for a multi-day summit of international consultations focused on countering rising global antisemitism, before extending their mission to Ireland on Tuesday.
The J7 coalition comprises major Jewish community organizations from the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, France, Germany, Australia, and Argentina. Formed in response to soaring rates of antisemitic incidents worldwide, the task force unites these Diaspora organizations to coordinate policy strategies, tech policy, security initiatives, and educational approaches against Jew hatred.
The multi-day summit comes as the J7’s latest annual report found that 2025 was the deadliest year for Jews living outside Israel since 1994, with the UK among the countries that recorded an increase in antisemitic incidents.
As part of the summit, delegates met with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband in London on Monday to press UK officials regarding government stances under new leader Andy Burnham.
The group expressed serious concern about recent UK Government measures and rhetoric targeting Israel and the detrimental impact this decision had on their own countries and communities.
Sharp rise in global antisemitism, Iranian regime threat, proliferation of hate
Representatives discussed the sharp rise in global antisemitism, the threat posed by the Iranian regime and its proxies, the growing proliferation of online hate, and the continued demonization of Israel, including in rhetoric, from many of those in elected office and public life, which all too often serves as a vehicle for antisemitic rhetoric, incitement, and behavior.
The J7 welcomed Miliband’s expression of the “abhorrence” of the motion against Zionism at the recent Green Party conference and his affirmation of the importance of the IHRA definition of antisemitism.
During the meeting, J7 leaders also proposed a new international ministerial task force on antisemitism and welcomed Miliband’s agreement to host an inaugural meeting.
ADL CEO and National Director Jonathan Greenblatt said, “We had a direct and productive conversation with Foreign Secretary Miliband. While there are areas of strong disagreement, we identified some common concerns, including our shared view on the bigoted anti-Zionism of the Green Party; the need to curb the wave of vicious harassment and hostile rhetoric directed at the British Jewish community; and the necessity of mitigating the expanding threat of online antisemitism enabled by AI and social media. But this was just the first conversation. We intend to keep pushing for action and demanding accountability.”
Following the meeting, Miliband said in a statement, “Antisemitism has no place in our society. Jewish communities must be able to live freely and safely, without fear of discrimination, abuse, or violence. The rise in antisemitic incidents across a number of countries demands a coordinated international response. Today’s discussion helped identify practical ways that governments, communities and international partners can work together to tackle antisemitism and share what works.”
As the summit began on Monday, UK Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood announced in Parliament a public inquiry into the murders of two men, Adrian Daulby and Melvin Cravitz, killed in a terror attack carried out by Jihad Al-Shamie at the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester on Yom Kippur in October 2025.
Continuing their mission on Tuesday, the task force traveled to Ireland and gathered in Dublin’s Herzog Park to stand in solidarity with the local Jewish community and raise concerns over rising antisemitic rhetoric and actions in the country.
Named in 1995 in honor of Israel’s sixth president Chaim Herzog, the son of Rabbi Yitzhak HaLevi Herzog, a former chief rabbi of Ireland (1921-1936), the park was the center of a heated national controversy in late November and December 2025, when a city council push to strip away Herzog’s name sparked opposition before being suspended and shelved.
'No Jew... should ever feel they must choose between being proudly Irish and proudly Jewish'
Addressing the gathering, Maurice Cohen, chairman of the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland, spoke about the historic vulnerability and resilience of the local community, telling the delegates, “We are a small community of just 2,200 people, but our roots in Ireland stretch back centuries. I can think of no more fitting place to welcome you than Herzog Park... The attempt to remove his name was deeply hurtful to our community and is typical of the ubiquitous, ambient antisemitism that reflects a growing hostility that Irish Jews increasingly encounter. No Jew in Ireland should ever feel they must choose between being proudly Irish and proudly Jewish.”
Cohen noted that between “July 2025 and January 2026, we recorded 143 antisemitic incidents, a deeply troubling number for a community of our size. We are grateful for the increased attention of An Garda Síochána, but we need more than expressions of concern. We need practical security measures, political leadership, and a clear recognition that antisemitism, whatever language it is dressed in, has no place in Irish society. We are not asking for special treatment.”
Delivering a statement on behalf of the J7, Jonathan Greenblatt told the delegates, “Today, we stand in solidarity with Ireland’s Jewish community and sound the alarm about antisemitic rhetoric and actions here in Ireland, before they escalate further.
As Maurice mentioned, of all the places we visited today, we chose to gather here in Herzog Park... Last year, a campaign to strip his name from this park was rightly condemned by Irish government leaders as an act that transcends political debate and instead targets Jewish memory itself.”
Greenblatt noted that although Ireland is not a J7 member country, the task force included a special chapter on Ireland in its latest annual report using data from the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland.
“Anti-Israel rhetoric in Ireland is creating an increasingly hostile environment for Ireland’s Jews, directly affecting the safety and daily lives of this small, historic Jewish community,” Greenblatt said.
“While Ireland’s national police have certainly increased their surveillance and security presence, there remains an urgent need for dedicated security funding for the Jewish community. Ireland cannot afford to wait for a tragedy before taking action. We are calling on the Irish Government to introduce concrete, preventative measures now. That means dedicated security funding for Jewish communal and educational institutions, consistent enforcement of hate crime legislation, and clear political accountability when rhetoric demonizes Jews or crosses the line into antisemitism,” Greenblatt said.
The J7 met with Irish Taoiseach, Micheal Martin, and Secretary General of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Joe Hackett.
The J7 said in a statement, “We've seen in our own countries how an increasingly hostile environment for Jews can lead to deadly violence, as we witnessed in Bondi, Manchester, Boulder and Washington D.C. The demonization of Israel generates and fuels the surge in antisemitism in Ireland and beyond.”
“We warned the Taoiseach and the Secretary General that the conditions for an antisemitic terrorist attack are sadly all too evident in Ireland, and Ireland cannot afford to wait for a tragedy before acting,” the J7 said.
The task force also met on Monday with the Union of Jewish Students in London as well as the Community Security Trust – which provides advice, training, representation, security services, and research to the UK’s Jewish Community – and will be meeting with government and Jewish leaders in the coming days.

Why You Should Do Toe Raises, Not Just Calf Raises
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:12:57 UTC
04:12:57 KST

Here’s a workout tip that sounds like it belongs in a nursery rhyme: Bring your toes toward your nose. That’s how physical therapist Joseph Hribick reminds patients to do toe raises. Fortunately, it’s not a flexibility test: Your toes don’t have to get anywhere near your face. Keep your heels on the floor, lift the fronts of your feet, and you’ll work the muscles along your shins.
“Each time we step, we need to be able to clear our toes from the ground,” says Hribick, a clinical assistant professor of physical therapy at Lebanon Valley College in Pennsylvania. Otherwise, your toes could snag on the carpet or catch as you walk through a doorway, making you more likely to trip.
If you’ve ever done calf raises, you know the opposite move: lifting your heels and rising onto the balls of your feet. Toe raises give the other side of your lower legs some attention. They require no equipment, you can do them while you’re sitting at your desk, and they can make your shins burn (in a good way) after surprisingly few reps.
What are the benefits of toe raises?
The star of the toe raise is the tibialis anterior, a muscle that runs along the front of your shin. It helps lift your foot as your leg swings forward—and then controls how your foot lowers after your heel touches the ground, Hribick says.
Your calves do the opposite job: They help push you forward. Daniel Safford, an assistant professor of physical therapy at Arcadia University in Pennsylvania, suggests giving both sides of your lower legs some attention. “You’re covering a lot of your bases if you do just those two things,” he says of calf raises and toe raises.
That can be especially useful if the muscles that lift your feet are weak. But will adding toe raises to your day make you a faster runner or keep you from falling? “That’s a little bit more of a question mark,” Safford says. Those muscles matter for walking and balance, but studies haven’t established that toe raises alone deliver those bigger benefits. Still, they’re a useful addition to a routine that also works your calves and challenges your balance.
How to do toe raises correctly
You can do toe raises sitting or standing; if your balance isn’t what it used to be, choose the chair. Plant both feet on the floor and lift the fronts of your feet while keeping your heels down. The balls of your feet should come up along with your toes—wiggling your toes alone doesn’t count. Take one to two seconds to lift, pause briefly, then two to three seconds to lower. “If you just bring your toes up and let them slam down, you’re not getting as much of a benefit,” Hribick says.
For a bigger challenge, try them standing. That means your legs are supporting your weight, and staying steady adds a challenge, so hold on to a sturdy counter. Lift the fronts of both feet at once. It’s fine to shift a little weight onto your heels, Safford says, but don’t lean your whole body backward to get your feet off the floor. Lift as high as you comfortably can; even if your feet barely budge, the muscles are still working.
Shoes or bare feet? Whichever you prefer. Barefoot, you may even get a glimpse of the exercise in action: Safford says the tendons can “kind of pop out on the top of the foot” as you lift, a bit like the tendons on the back of your hand.
How many toe raises should you do—and how often?
Start with five to 10 repetitions a few days a week, Safford suggests. That might sound almost too easy, but try a set before you decide. “You might feel more fatigued than you’d expect,” Hribick says.
As your shins get used to the exercise, add a few reps. Safford says you could eventually work up to 20 repetitions on most days of the week, but give yourself a couple of months to get there. “You don’t wanna go for broke,” he says. Mild soreness is possible when you start; if you have pain that’s severe or won’t go away, stop and get it checked out. The same goes for a new problem lifting your foot or toes that keep catching on the floor.
The best part about toe raises is that you can do them almost anywhere. Try a set at your desk, or do them standing at the bathroom sink. “You could do it when you’re brushing your teeth,” Safford says. “Just hold on to the counter.”

BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge and chief minister DK Shivakumar Tuesday reiterated that peaceful protest is fundamental to democracy and promised a review of police action against anti-SIR demonstrators in Bengaluru.Activists, however, said assurances were not enough and demanded the withdrawal of the police licensing order restricting protests to Freedom Park and restoration of the 2009 order governing assemblies and processions.The demand follows Monday’s detention of protesters who had gathered near KR Circle to march to the chief electoral officer’s office against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police detained them after they refused to move to Freedom Park, while photojournalists covering the action were also allegedly manhandled.Kharge said he had instructed police to ensure peaceful demonstrations were not disrupted. Shivakumar said he had sought a full report on the circumstances leading to the police action and warned that accountability would follow if there had been unnecessary use of force or excess.
“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. We cannot demand that right for ourselves in Delhi and deny it to others in Bengaluru,” Shivakumar said, adding that there would be “no double standards”. He, along with Kharge, was in Delhi on Monday to protest against SIR.Activists welcomed the assurances but said the govt must address the restrictions that, they argue, make it difficult to protest at the site of an issue or draw public attention to local grievances.“The Licensing Order, 2021 by the commissioner of police restricting protests to Freedom Park must be withdrawn, just as any restriction to designated venues for protests in any city. Protests cannot be caged in Freedom Park; holding placards and shouting slogans cannot be criminalised; peaceful marches cannot be met with police violence,” advocate and activist Clifton Rozario said.He added that police power could not be used against legitimate struggles in defence of the Constitution.My Vote, My Right, which had organised Monday’s protest march, welcomed Kharge’s decision to review the police handling of protesters and journalists, but urged the govt to withdraw the 2021 licensing order and restore the “2009 assemblies order”. The organisation also questioned Shivakumar over what it saw as a contradiction between his participation in a protest in Delhi and the action against demonstrators in Bengaluru, asking: “One law for you, one law for us — why?”A woman protester who was forcibly dragged away by police on Monday said restricting demonstrations to Freedom Park curtailed citizens’ rights. “This rule is what allows the police to deem any protest outside the said venue, even if it is barely a kilometre away, illegitimate,” she said.Activists under the Horatada Hakkigagi Janandolana said the restriction had also affected people seeking to raise local issues. A protest over a neighbourhood grievance, they argued, loses its immediate relevance when residents must travel to a central venue to be heard. They have cited workers, farmers, pourakarmikas, Dalit activists and residents protesting civic issues among those whose demonstrations have been affected.The coalition was, as of late Tuesday, preparing a fresh memorandum to the govt. On the same as the CM and Kharge’s assurances, Bengaluru police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh said KR Circle was a heavily congested junction and police had asked protesters to shift to Freedom Park. He said the protesters refused and blocked the road, following which police removed the blockade and made preventive arrests.Acknowledging a confrontation involving protesters, police and media personnel, Singh described it as unintentional and said officers had been instructed to exercise utmost care. He maintained that the right to protest in Bengaluru was, under the court’s order, limited to Freedom Park, and said police were prepared to provide protection when informed in advance.
Activists insist that reviewing Monday’s police action must go hand in hand with changing the rules governing where people can demonstrate. They want the govt to withdraw the 2021 order and restore the 2009 framework, under which they say protests could be held at different locations after informing the police.

Zelensky claims West gave no warning of latest Russian strike
Ukraine received no advance warning from its Western partners ahead of an overnight Russian missile strike, Vladimir Zelensky claimed on Tuesday.
The Ukrainian Air Force first raised the issue earlier in the day, saying it detected incoming missiles only during their final approach, without receiving advance intelligence from the West.
Footage circulating online appeared to show at least six ballistic missiles striking Kiev, with air raid sirens sounding only after the impacts.
Zelensky echoed the complaint, saying Ukraine had received no warning from its “partners” about the impending attack. He did not single out any country but stressed that Western intelligence on planned Russian strikes remains “one of the most critical issues” for Kiev.
The presumed lack of the early warning sparked speculation that the US might have stopped sharing intelligence with Kiev. The two countries have been engaged in a public spat over the past few days. Zelensky condemned the US decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel as a “weak decision by strong partners,” while US President Donald Trump suggested it is time for Ukraine to get a “new president” instead of Zelensky, whose tenure has long ended but no elections have been held under the pretext of the conflict with Russia.
Trump has appeared to reject the allegations that Washington stopped sharing intelligence with Kiev, stating the US has been working with both Russia and Ukraine “on getting the war to end.”
“We are helping them, and we are sharing intel,” Trump told reporters.
Kiev usually receives early missile warnings through the Battlespace Command and Control Center, a system used by the US military and the NATO bloc. Media reports have suggested the presumed lack of warning overnight was an isolated technical incident rather than a political decision. A source familiar with the matter told Politico that the US had told Ukraine that there was “no warning because of bad weather conditions.” Kiev, however, was reportedly unsatisfied with the explanation and that a “growing number of people” are concerned that there were other reasons behind the lack of warning.

EU watchdog urges smart glasses to clearly signal when recording
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:11:09 UTC
04:11:09 KST

EU watchdog urges smart glasses to clearly signal when recording
Advisory comes amid growing concern about the devices being used to secretly record girls and women.
The European Union’s data watchdog has called for smart glasses to clearly show when they are recording, saying bystanders have the right to know when they are being photographed or filmed.
The European Data Protection Board (EDPB) issued the non-binding recommendation on Tuesday, amid mounting concern about the devices being used to secretly record girls and women.
It said the use of smart glasses – which can resemble ordinary glasses but also take photos and videos, make phone calls and translate text when connected to the internet – raises “serious privacy concerns”.
EDPB chair Anu Talus said the glasses should have clear signals when they are recording, such as “bright LED lights, audio signals or voice activation cues, privacy-friendly smartphone notifications, or unique designs”.
“These warnings need to be reliable, hard to ignore, and always up to date,” said Talus. “Even in public spaces, bystanders should clearly understand that someone is filming or photographing them.”
The devices carry greater risks in “sensitive” spaces like schools and hospitals, as well as public spots like beaches, and raised concerns about children who are “more vulnerable to covert or intrusive processing of their personal data”, the EDPB warned.
The advisory comes amid campaigns in several European countries to ban or restrict smart glasses over privacy concerns.
Norway’s government said last week it was also worried about privacy invasions and wants a temporary ban on the use of smart glasses in certain public places. The capital Oslo already opted to ban glasses equipped with cameras in schools.
France’s e-Enfance association, which operates the national hotline for victims of online abuse, has also sounded the alarm about videos recorded with camera-equipped glasses and shared online.
Last month, French prosecutors said they had opened a criminal probe following sexual harassment complaints related to a social media trend of using smart glasses to film women on the street, without their consent, and posting the videos online.
In the United Kingdom and Ireland, a “Stop Smart Glasses” campaign has launched a petition and call for supporters to contact stores to stop their sale. It reached more than 10,000 signatures, which means the UK government must respond.

African resources 'belong to Africa': China's Xi
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:06:15 UTC
04:06:15 KST

Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that African mineral resources "belong to Africa", offering Beijing's support for the industry and warning against "geopolitical rivalries" that could harm it.
China, through state-owned and private businesses, is a key player in Africa's valuable mining sector, particularly in extraction. It is one of several major powers vying for access to resources.
Accepting "the principle that African resources belong to Africa must be a prerequisite for any cooperation", Xi said during a meeting in Beijing on Tuesday with Botswana's President Duma Boko, whose country has a vast mining industry.
"Africa has been relegated to the bottom of the industrial chain and of the value chain by an unjust international division of labour. This is a historical injustice that requires urgent remedy," Xi said, according to official news agency Xinhua.
The Chinese leader called for balance between "moral principles and economic interests", while offering his country's assistance in drawing up development plans.
African countries hold around 30 per cent of the world's critical mineral reserves, including cobalt, copper, lithium, nickel and rare earths, according to the United Nations, making it a focus of competition between the United States and China for strategic resources. European nations and other actors are also competing for influence.
Xi, in his remarks, said that "African resources must not become instruments of geopolitical rivalries", calling for all foreign powers involved to "contribute sincerely to Africa's development" and help maintain a "stable" environment for cooperation.
China is Africa's largest trading partner and a major source of financing for infrastructure projects across the continent.
On May 1, Beijing extended a zero-tariff policy to all African countries except Eswatini, with which it has no diplomatic relations, under a policy announced last year.
Some critics accuse foreign actors including China of exploiting African resources without allowing the countries and their people to truly benefit from them.
Hailing his country's commitment to "African development", Xi said Beijing seeks to steer Sino-African mineral cooperation towards greater "industrial added value".

Pope Leo’s lung operation ‘successfully completed’: Vatican
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:05:30 UTC
04:05:30 KST

Pope Leo’s lung operation ‘successfully completed’: Vatican
ROME - Pope Leo XIV’s operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital to remove a nodule from his lung was “successfully completed”, the Vatican said on Oct 13.
The pope had entered the hospital smiling and waving the morning of Oct 13, hours before the surgery to remove the growth that looks like a coin on the lung.
“The procedure was successfully completed, within the expected time and in the planned manner,” the Vatican said in a brief statement.
“The Holy Father has returned to his room,” it said, adding that more details would be given later.
The surgery marks the 71-year-old Leo’s first hospitalisation since he became head of the Catholic Church on May 8, 2025. Vatican officials who saw the pope on Oct 12 said he appeared relaxed about the hospital stay.
In a surprise announcement following Angelus prayers on Oct 11, Pope Leo told crowds in St Peter’s Square that doctors had discovered the nodule “at a very early stage” during medical checks.
“The doctors believe it would be right to intervene,” he said.
The Vatican has historically been very secretive about the health of popes, but began to be more transparent during the illness of Leo’s predecessor Francis, an Argentine who freely discussed his ailments.
People outside the hospital expressed concern over the pope’s condition.
Giorgia Fei, a 57-year-old Italian, said she had been worried by the news.
“However, the Holy Father is in very good hands here at the hospital because we have some outstanding doctors,” she said.
“I will pray a lot for him.”
Giuseppe Purpura, 72, said he was also concerned.
“He’s still quite young and I really wasn’t expecting this. I thought he was in better health,” he said, noting that “thankfully it was caught in time.”
The Vicar General for the Diocese of Rome, Cardinal Baldassare Reina, led a rosary prayer for the pope inside the hospital chapel which was broadcast by the Vatican. Dozens of people attended and Reina asked all the city’s parishes to join in.
Ahead of the surgery, the Vatican said the pope’s recovery time was expected to be about a week. His audiences have been cancelled until Oct 20.
The Vatican secretary of state, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told ANSA news agency that Leo had been “very calm” about his condition when they met on Monday.
Routine health checks
Chicago-born Leo, the first US pope, is sporty and believed to generally be in good health.
He is scheduled to travel to South America from Nov 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
It was not immediately clear what would happen if the pope was forced into a longer recovery.
Under Church law, a figure known as the Cardinal Camerlengo – or chamberlain – takes over administrative duties if the pope dies, but pontiffs do not have a deputy to replace them if they become incapacitated.
Marco Scarci, a thoracic surgery expert in the UK, told AFP it was not “a particularly risky operation” and he expected Leo’s recovery to be quick.
Most pulmonary nodules are benign, or non-cancerous, but a small percentage can be an early indication of lung cancer.
The Vatican told AFP the nodule was found during routine health checks, and there were no symptoms that led to checking the pope’s lungs.
‘Coin lesion’
A small nodule is called a “coin lesion” because on X-rays it looks like a coin, Professor Federico Venuta, head of thoracic surgery at the Policlinico Umberto 1 hospital in Rome, told AFP.
Small nodules tend not to cause symptoms, but larger ones can cause shortness of breath, chest pain and persistent coughing – sometimes with blood.
Such nodules “could be a whole range of benign lesions – inflammatory, infectious, autoimmune, or congenital – or they could be malignant,” Venuta said.
Removing the nodule can take place under general anaesthetic with the patient breathing through a tube.
Even if the nodule was not benign, the pope’s outlook would be “very positive”, Venuta said.
“For a generally healthy person, the prognosis for lung cancer caught at such an early stage – specifically a pulmonary nodule with no distant spread – is absolutely favourable,” he said. AFP

TOI explains: Why can’t Bengaluru protest outside Freedom Park?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
19:02:25 UTC
04:02:25 KST

A Karnataka high court order and a police licensing regime have made Freedom Park Bengaluru’s default protest venue. But the governing police order also gives the police commissioner discretion to designate another suitable venue, meaning the legal position is more nuanced than an absolute ban on demonstrations elsewhere. Here’s everything you need to know about why Bengaluru cannot protest outside Freedom Park:Bengaluru has confined protests to Freedom Park. The practice emerged from a suo motu Karnataka High Court case initiated in 2021 over the effect of demonstrations on traffic and the rights of people not participating in them.How did the restriction begin?On March 3, 2022, a division bench of the Karnataka High Court passed an interim order directing the state government to ensure that no protests, processions and similar activities were held anywhere in Bengaluru except at Freedom Park, Gandhinagar. The court also directed that such activities be organised without adversely affecting traffic, especially during rush hours, and that action be taken where traffic was disrupted.On August 1, 2022, the High Court disposed of the case. In paragraph 4, it recorded a submission that protests, marches and dharnas would be permitted only at Freedom Park, and that the state was obliged to ensure compliance with the 2021 licensing order.
In paragraph 5, the operative direction required authorities to ensure compliance with that order “in letter and spirit” and to continue action against those violating it.What does the police order say?The Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021, published in the state gazette in January 2022, is the rule currently governing protests in Bengaluru. It says no protests, demonstrations, dharnas or protest marches may be held in the city without a licence under the order.Clause 4.1 identifies Freedom Park as the venue for protests in Bengaluru. However, it also says that, depending on the situation, the commissioner of police may designate any other suitable place in the city for that purpose. The licensing authority may approve the number of participants at Freedom Park based on the type of programme, duration and available capacity.So, are protests outside Freedom Park illegal?Not necessarily in every circumstance. The 2021 order does not expressly prohibit protest marches, nor does it state that Freedom Park is the only possible venue: it identifies Freedom Park while preserving the police commissioner’s discretion to designate another suitable location.A legal backgrounder prepared by activists argues that the High Court’s final order did not itself direct that protests be held only at Freedom Park; it directed compliance with the licensing order. On that reading, the court’s judgment does not prevent rallies and does not mandate Freedom Park as the sole venue.The distinction matters because the March 2022 interim order did expressly restrict protests and processions to Freedom Park, while the August 2022 final order required enforcement of the 2021 licensing rules. The two must be read alongside the licensing order before drawing a definitive legal conclusion.
Why does this matter?Activists argue that concentrating demonstrations at one venue reduces their visibility and makes it harder for groups to draw public attention to local grievances. The backgrounder says the restrictions have affected workers, farmers, Dalit activists, sanitation workers and residents seeking to protest on issues in their own localities.The debate is ultimately about balancing traffic management and public convenience with the constitutional right to assemble peacefully and express dissent. For now, Freedom Park remains Bengaluru’s designated and practically dominant protest venue. Whether the police commissioner’s discretion to permit demonstrations elsewhere is exercised, and on what terms, remains central to the controversy.
Chethan Kumar is a Senior Assistant Editor with the Times of India. Aside from specialising in Space & Science, he has reported extensively on varied topics, with special focus on defence, policy and data stories. He has covered multiple elections, too. As a young democracy grows out of adolescence, Chethan feels, there are reels of tales emerging which need to be captured. To do this, he alternates between the mundane goings-on of the Common Man and the wonder-filled worlds of scientists and scamsters, politicians and soldiers. In a career spanning nearly 18 years, he has reported from multiple datelines — Houston, Florida, Kochi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Sriharikota (AP), NH-1 (J&K Highway), New Delhi, Ahmedabad, Raichur, Bhatkal, Mysuru, Chamarajanagar, to name a few — but is based out of Bengaluru, India’s science capital that also hosts the ISRO HQ.

Ukraine will become an agricultural part of the EU under special conditions: Brussels outlines the future of grain exports
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
22:01:04 EEST
04:01:04 KST

Ukraine will become an agricultural part of the EU under special conditions: Brussels outlines the future of grain exports
Kyiv • UNN
The EU may restrict access for certain Ukrainian agricultural products to its market. The final terms will be determined during accession negotiations.
After joining the European Union, Ukraine will become part of the EU's common agricultural policy, but special conditions may be introduced for its agricultural sector. European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos stated this while speaking with journalists on October 13 in Luxembourg, UNN reports, citing the European Commission.
In particular, Brussels proposes preserving the focus of Ukrainian grain exports on traditional markets in North Africa, the Middle East and other Asian countries, while restricting access for certain types of agricultural products to the European market.
Details
According to Kos, integrating Ukraine's agricultural sector into the European Union will require a special approach because of the scale of agricultural production in Ukraine and its competitiveness. The European commissioner explained that the proposed mechanism must simultaneously take into account the interests of European farmers and ensure opportunities for the further development of Ukrainian agricultural exports.
We must protect European farmers. And secondly, we must help Ukrainian agriculture develop so that it can export its products throughout the world, especially grain and wheat. Of course, Ukrainian producers must also be ready to comply with all European standards
She noted that the European Commission proposes applying targeted special arrangements that should be taken into account when preparing the future treaty on Ukraine's accession to the EU. The final parameters of such a mechanism have not yet been determined. They are expected to be agreed upon as part of negotiations between Ukraine and the European Union.
Kos also drew attention to the need to protect European funding, in particular the funds allocated to support agriculture.
Why the EU is proposing special conditions for Ukraine
On October 6, the European Commission presented a package of proposals to prepare the European Union for future enlargement. The document devoted particular attention to Ukraine's agricultural sector.
In Brussels, they believe that the considerable scale of production and high productivity of Ukrainian agriculture require special integration mechanisms. In particular, the European Commission proposed significantly limiting financial support and access to the European market for certain sensitive categories of Ukrainian agricultural products.
At the same time, the EU should help Ukraine restore its presence in traditional foreign markets. These primarily include the countries of North Africa and the Middle East, which have historically purchased significant volumes of Ukrainian grain.
In this way, Brussels seeks to avoid a situation in which, after Ukraine joins the EU, large volumes of Ukrainian agricultural products are redirected to the bloc's domestic market and intensify competition for local producers.
What Ukraine's position will be
The Ukrainian side has already expressed reservations about the possible introduction of permanent restrictions on agricultural exports after accession to the EU.
Ukraine's Minister of Agrarian Policy and Food Taras Vysotskyi previously stated that Kyiv was ready to discuss transitional periods for adapting the agricultural sector, but did not agree to an indefinite restriction on access for Ukrainian products to the European market. According to him, temporary mechanisms could be part of the negotiation process, but permanent restrictions would contradict the principle of full membership in the European Union.
The Ukrainian side also emphasizes that any special conditions for sensitive agricultural goods, including their list, the duration of restrictions and possible mechanisms for supporting producers, must be determined exclusively during accession negotiations.
When the final conditions may become known
The integration of Ukraine's agricultural sector will be considered within negotiation cluster No. 5, which covers agriculture, resources and cohesion. The European Commission plans to take into account the specific features of Ukrainian agricultural production when formulating the EU's position on opening the relevant negotiation cluster.
At the same time, Marta Kos had previously emphasized that special conditions for agriculture do not mean introducing a separate or inferior format of Ukraine’s membership in the European Union.
We remind you
Ukrainian agricultural associations insist on a 10-year transition period after Ukraine joins the EU, so that adaptation to European directives does not lead to a reduction in production, billions in losses, and weakened competitiveness of the sector.

US Army unveils new warfighting guidance to align with evolving battlefield threats
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
18:58:15 UTC
03:58:15 KST

Diyar Güldoğan
13 October 2026•Update: 13 October 2026
The US Army is introducing new operational warfighting guidance designed to align its doctrine, training, force structure, and technology investments with evolving battlefield threats, Gen. Christopher LaNeve, vice army chief of Staff, said Tuesday.
Speaking at the Association of the United States Army’s Eisenhower Luncheon, LaNeve, who is also serving as acting army chief of staff, outlined the army’s new guidance, How the Army Fights, which was published last week.
The document is intended to establish a common framework for how the army contributes to joint military operations, drawing lessons from conflicts including Russia’s war in Ukraine and fighting in the Middle East.
"Upfront, I’ll just say, How the Army Fights is not a departure from Multi-Domain Operations. The purpose of this document is to provide warfighting guidance that enables every single leader to understand their role in Multi-Domain Operations," he said.
LaNeve said the changing battlefield, characterized by widespread unmanned aerial systems, persistent surveillance, increasingly precise long-range fires, and the growing importance of cyber and space capabilities, requires the army to adapt how it fights.
He outlined four interconnected elements at the heart of the new guidance: convergence, strike, close battle, and endurance.
"Together, these four elements of land power provide the US Army, within the Joint Force, the ability to fight and win our nation’s wars," he said.
The army plans to expand the integration of autonomous and unmanned systems across its formations, including the introduction of military occupational specialties focused on unmanned aerial systems and robotics.
LaNeve also announced that the Futures and Concepts Command had been redesignated the US Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command, or FASCOM, following the establishment of the Autonomous Warfare Command.
"The army is not turning its back on modernization. We are sprinting towards (it)," he said.
LaNeve called on defense industry partners to support army efforts to field effective technologies at scale, stressing that innovation must be linked directly to battlefield requirements.
The ultimate objective, he said, is to preserve the Army’s position as the world’s leading land power and ensure it remains prepared to respond whenever the nation calls.

Israelis aren’t afraid of Iran, they’re afraid of supermarket prices, Zelekha says - interview
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-13
18:57:46 UTC
03:57:46 KST

The Economic Party leader promises sweeping changes to living costs within three months of becoming finance minister—and threatens to bring down any government that gets in his way.
Israel’s young people have faced Iran, Hezbollah, and Hamas, but the price of filling a shopping cart still frightens them, Economic Party leader Yaron Zelekha told The Jerusalem Post on Tuesday.
“Our young people deserve to live, not just survive. They are not afraid of the Iranians. They were not afraid of Hezbollah or Hamas. But they are afraid of a trip to the supermarket.”
Their mothers, he added, fear their children will leave Israel because they cannot afford to buy a home. Those pressures drive his campaign to become finance minister - and, he warned, keeping a government together would not take priority over addressing them.
“If anyone gets in my way, I will bring down their government,” he said, stating he would demand control of the Finance Ministry and the Competition Authority in coalition negotiations.
It is a warning he would apply to either political bloc. Whether Benjamin Netanyahu, Naftali Bennett, or Gadi Eisenkot becomes prime minister, Zelekha said he would insist on the authority to implement his economic program and would be prepared to bring down the government if obstructed.
Zelekha’s five-step plan to lower cost of living as soon as he takes the helm
His opening offer to voters is equally bold: five measures to tackle living costs, with a difference households would feel within three months of his taking office.
“I plan to take five steps as the opening move in a fight against the cost of living that will last throughout the government’s term,” Zelekha said.
The first two would abolish all tariffs, without exception, and eliminate import quotas.
The third would prevent monopolies in domestic production from also acting as importers. Zelekha argued that companies operating in both markets use their control of imports to block competition against their locally produced goods.
His fourth measure would prohibit exclusive import agreements and prevent an importer controlling imports from one major international manufacturer from also taking control of imports from another manufacturer that should compete with it.
Finally, he would move the Competition Authority into the Finance Ministry, placing it under his supervision so that he could oversee enforcement of competition law.
Zelekha described the package as an opening intervention that would produce a significant change on its own, followed by further reforms throughout the government’s term.
Asked how quickly people would notice the difference, he gave a timeline of months, not years.
“Within three months from the day I take my seat, you will not recognize the country,” he said.
Zelekha further insisted that his premise would not require any funding, and would actually generate money.
Like its citizens, the government also pays inflated prices for its purchases, he argued. Meanwhile, households spending more on necessities have less money available for other economic activity, slowing the economy and limiting growth in tax revenues.
Lowering those costs, he maintained, would benefit public finances as well as consumers.
Zelekha’s willingness to negotiate with either bloc comes with an insistence that the identity of the prime minister would not change his economic strategy.
“None of them will change my strategy, because implementing it will be entrusted to me. I will be finance minister, and I will not allow any of them to interfere.”
If a prime minister obstructed him, he said, he would not hesitate to bring down the government and move to the opposing bloc. He presented his independence from both camps as a source of negotiating power.
“Although my positions are right-wing, my conditions are substantive matters of principle.”
Beyond control of the Finance Ministry and Competition Authority, Zelekha set two further conditions.
“We will not sit in a government that includes Arab parties, and we will not sit in a government that allows draft evasion.”
He called for Arabs to perform national service and haredim to serve in the military, saying the state should create frameworks that allow haredi recruits to preserve their religious beliefs.
Those arrangements, he said, should be accompanied by higher pay for regular soldiers and better conditions for reservists. At the same time, he argued that people avoiding service should not continue receiving state benefits.
For Zelekha, demanding broader participation in service also means finding the money to support those who serve. He criticized an approach that relies on aggressive rhetoric against population groups without providing the resources needed to improve daily life.
A partnership rooted in rejecting the status quo
That connection between service and economic policy is central to his partnership with Yoaz Hendel, which Zelekha said followed more than half a year of discussions.
“Neither of us is willing to let the status quo continue.”
He described their shared objective as shaking a system in which some benefit from connections between wealth and political power while others maintain arrangements allowing them to avoid military service.
Hendel, he said, brings plans to improve reservists’ conditions and establish military frameworks capable of accommodating haredim. Zelekha would seek the financial resources to implement them.
Asked whether either had made concessions to establish the alliance, he said their agendas reinforced each other. Both, he added, hold right-wing positions, oppose a Palestinian state, and support strengthening settlement in the West Bank.
Zelekha pointed to the haredi campus at Ono Academic College as an example of a framework that allowed students to enter the workforce while maintaining their religious identity. He argued that suitable military frameworks could follow the same principle.
“But those plans require money. I know how to bring in the money.”

Saudi Arabia issues warning to Houthis over attacks on airports, holy cities
